I wrote the Session 4 deck, `slides.md` and `INSTRUCTOR.md`, and opened the deck in your browser. Nothing is committed yet; the repo is still on `main`.

**Deck (`sessions/session-4/deck/index.html`)**
- **Built on Session 2's deck:** it reuses Session 2's code and styles (same colors, mascot, animated route and chat) and the kurasu slides API, so it can run inside the classroom the same way.
- **20 slides with concepts only.** Under the usual opening (title, agenda, recap questions, cognitive debt and surrender), the concept slides follow a mini route of five stops:
  - **el proyecto:** `AGENTS.md` as an index, and what goes in each place (AGENTS.md, docs, invariants, wiki).
  - **el problema:** the problem domain, one problem with many solutions, the agent asking the decisions one at a time with a decision tree.
  - **la solución:** model, screens, flows and prototypes.
  - **documentar:** living documents, the two templates for the homework, the doc as the review criterion.
  - **subagentes:** one context per job, and the brief as everything the subagent knows.
  - **closing:** cost, when not to use AI, ownership, recap, and what comes next (homework, Session 5 demos, the move to the advanced sessions).
- **Example:** the concept slides use the multi-user to-do list from the earlier sessions, not the chat, so they don't answer ahead of time the questions the room will answer live.
- **Checks:** I screenshotted every slide in a headless browser and fixed the overflows and overlaps I found. I didn't step through every animation click by click; the browser is the place to check that.

**`slides.md`:** one entry per deck slide, in the same order, with the animation clicks in the speaker notes.

**`INSTRUCTOR.md`**
- No timing. It states the format: concept slides, then the live mahou run on the classroom chat, with questions answered as they come up.
- For each block, it lists the concept and what to do live. The project block walks through `app/AGENTS.md` → `docs/` → invariants → prototypes → `.mahou/wiki`. In shape, the room answers the questions, and the scope is set up front as "chat for the featured session".
- An "Antes de la clase" section covers the dry run, keeping its artifacts as a fallback, deploying kurasu if you use a poll, and screen hygiene.

**Still out of date**
- `exercise/README.md` still describes the two in-class practice blocks; under the new format they're the homework.
- `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` still says Session 4 introduces subagents.

Both are listed under Pendientes in `INSTRUCTOR.md`. I can update them next, and commit everything on a branch when you're happy with the deck.

🎯

El problema

qué necesita quien lo va a usar: la parte de la realidad que el sistema tiene que atender

se describe sin nombrar el sistema
→→→
🧩

Una solución

el sistema que atiende esa necesidad

otra solución posible
otra más

Si arrancás por la solución, la elige el agente: la respuesta promedio de todo lo que ya vio.

Es la separación de siempre entre requerimientos y diseño: importa con o sin IA.

🎯 Definir el problema: mapear la realidad

Lo que buscamos entender antes de pensar en el sistema:

👥

Actores

quién está involucrado y qué rol cumple
🔗

Entidades

qué cosas existen en ese mundo y cómo se relacionan
🔄

Procesos

qué hace cada actor, en qué orden y qué dispara cada paso
📏

Reglas

lo que siempre tiene que cumplirse, y sus excepciones

Lo que buscamos decidir antes de escribir código, cada decisión con su porqué:

🗃️

Modelo

las entidades, sus campos, sus relaciones y dónde vive cada dato

sesión 1 ── n pregunta

los pasos de cada interacción: quién le pide qué a quién, y en qué orden

click → API → base → todos

borrador → abierta → cerrada

Componentes

las piezas del sistema, qué hace cada una y cómo se hablan

web ⇄ api ⇄ tiempo real

Pantallas

qué se ve, qué se puede hacer, y qué pasa mientras carga o cuando falla

cargando · listo · error

### [Agus] Tier 4: Context Engineering
- Problem domain vs. solution domain: the same feature described as a need (actors, data and relations, processes, in problem terms) and as a system (data diagrams, breadboards/page sketches, flows). Starting from the solution means deciding without having considered the problem in depth, and inheriting the agent's average answer for every decision left open.

- Cognitive debt and cognitive surrender: the cost of repeatedly delegating reasoning to the AI, and adopting its decisions as your own opinions
- When to delegate vs. intervene (developing intuition)
- Professional accountability: you sign off on what the AI produces
- Orchestration, in passing: shared docs as the ground truth that lets several agents work in parallel
- Cost and limits: tokens as a budget, model tiering, when NOT to use AI, skill atrophy, and what skills matter in an AI-augmented world.
